page: Microsoft Azure HB368-96rs_v5 is an x86_64 High Performance Computing instance built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by a dedicated Intel processor, the instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs alongside 448.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 4.67 GB of RAM per core. The architecture supports Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) capabilities and Premium Storage configurations, facilitating low-latency inter-node communication for tightly coupled compute workflows.

A key hardware characteristic of the HB368-96rs_v5 is its integrated high-capacity local storage subsystem. The instance bundles 15,874 GB of high-speed local NVMe solid-state storage directly on the host, eliminating dependence on external network-attached volumes for scratch space. The system does not feature dedicated GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing all host resources toward dense compute and heavy local disk I/O throughput.

By providing a massive 15.8 TB local NVMe footprint combined with 96 dedicated compute cores, the server offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive simulation workflows that would otherwise require multiple smaller instances or expensive external storage provisionings. The primary trade-off is the lack of hardware accelerators like GPUs and absent public IPv4 addressing. The configuration is engineered for high-performance computing, large-scale scientific simulations, clustered engineering analysis, and high-throughput scratch database operations.
description: Microsoft Azure HB368-96rs_v5 is a high-performance computing server instance engineered for intensive compute and high-capacity local storage requirements. Powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel processing cores managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the platform supplies 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 448.0 GB of RAM, offering approximately 4.67 GB of memory per core. The instance incorporates 15,874 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and supports Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) alongside Premium Storage capabilities. Because it includes no discrete GPUs and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance dedicates its entire hardware profile to CPU-bound execution and local file processing. This combination presents an efficient hardware density for tightly coupled parallel computing without incurring external network storage costs. The HB368-96rs_v5 is suited for large-scale engineering simulations, high-performance computing clusters, complex scientific modeling, and I/O-intensive scratch data analysis.
